findings.title: New CLIENTS resource type/scopes are never created for realms that already have an admin-permissions client
findings.body: init() only performs the full setup (creating scopes and the per-resource-type 'all-resource' resources, including the newly added CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE scopes CONFIGURE/MANAGE/MAP_ROLES/MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE/MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE/VIEW and the 'Clients' resource) when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is null; otherwise it returns immediately (lines 226-228). Any realm that already enabled ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 before this PR already has a non-null admin permissions client, so after upgrading, init() will no-op for that realm and the new 'Clients' scopes/resource will never be created. As a result the whole new Clients permission feature is silently non-functional (and, combined with the missing null-check described elsewhere, can throw NPEs) for any realm that adopted V2 admin permissions prior to this change. There is no migration logic added to retrofit the new resource type/scopes into already-provisioned admin-permission resource servers.

findings.title: NullPointerException risk when the 'Clients' all-resource type resource is missing
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), when no per-client resource exists, the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and immediately calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without checking whether the returned resource is null. getResourceTypeResource can legitimately return null (e.g. unsupported schema, or the 'Clients' resource not yet created for pre-existing admin-permission realms, see the related init() migration gap). Passing a null resource into findByResource is very likely to throw an NPE in the underlying store implementation, causing permission evaluation (canManage, canConfigure, canView, canMapRoles, etc. for a specific client) to fail with an unhandled exception instead of gracefully denying access.

findings.title: Cleanup listener for removed clients/roles/groups is now skipped entirely when only V2 admin permissions are enabled
findings.body: The ProviderEventListener body (handling RoleContainerModel.RoleRemovedEvent, ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent, GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent) is now wrapped in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))`, i.e. it only runs for the legacy V1 feature. Previously it ran unconditionally. This change appears necessary because, under V2, ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled/isPermissionsEnabled throw UnsupportedOperationException, which would otherwise crash on every client removal when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. However, by gating the whole handler behind the V1 flag instead of adding an equivalent V2 cleanup path, no corresponding cleanup of V2 authorization resources happens when a client, role, or group is deleted while only V2 is enabled. This leaves orphaned 'Clients'/'Users' resources and related policies referencing deleted entities in the authorization store, a data-integrity regression with no compensating implementation added in this PR.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission queries resources by type, but per-client resources are created without their type being set
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission() calls resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) to enumerate per-client resources. However, AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() (server-spi-private/.../AdminPermissionsSchema.java) creates the individual client resource via resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId()) and only calls resource.updateScopes(...); it never calls resource.setType(resourceType). Only the pre-created 'all-resource' resources built in init() have their type explicitly set. Unless the resource type is populated some other way, findByType will not match the individual per-client resources, so getClientsWithPermission() would return an incomplete/incorrect result (at best only the 'all-clients' aggregate resource, whose name is the literal string 'Clients', not a real client id).

findings.title: canList() javadoc references QUERY_USERS role which is unrelated to listing clients
findings.body: The newly added javadoc for canList() states: 'Or if the caller has at least one of the AdminRoles#QUERY_CLIENTS or AdminRoles#QUERY_USERS roles.' This appears to be a copy/paste mistake from the analogous Users permission evaluator documentation; QUERY_USERS has no obvious relation to listing clients and is likely to mislead readers about the actual authorization requirements for this method.

findings.title: Roles created in testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient are not cleaned up
findings.body: This test creates a client role ('myclient-role') and a sub-role ('myclient-subRole') directly via the admin API but, unlike similar tests elsewhere in this PR (e.g. UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.testMapRoles, which registers realm.cleanup().add(...) for the created role), it registers no cleanup. If the managed realm/test fixtures are reused across test methods in this class, the created roles and their composite relationship will persist beyond the test, which can affect subsequent tests or leave stale data.
